decision_basis.local_context: Clayton is at the Bukit Kiara carpark after returning from family travel on 2026-07-24 night.
decision_basis.physical_readiness: Yellow/caution: 5.03 hours primary sleep, but wake Body Battery 75, current Body Battery 48, HRV 50 ms balanced, resting HR 46 versus 48 seven-day average, no illness, and body feel great.
decision_basis.cns_interpretation: Acute short-sleep amber with fresh mental clarity and no brain fog; use a consequence-sensitive field gate rather than automatic CNS compromise.
decision_basis.density: No recorded training in the preceding seven days; ACWR 0.1 LOW represents underload rather than overload.
decision_basis.route_selection: Pure Quill is the smoothest and most familiar Twin Peaks enduro stage, so it is the appropriate controlled transfer surface. TnT, Flintstone, the full DH Line, 2K+, and novelty are excluded.
decision_basis.architecture_correction: A deterministic 5.0-to-under-5.5-hour sleep ceiling had converted short sleep alone into compromised CNS and a blanket trail ban; the revised graded rule preserves uncertainty while allowing bounded familiar skill after a clean field gate.

session.title: Kiara acute-short-sleep familiar skill gate
session.purpose: Restore one bike-specific and trail-specific touch after travel while testing whether current cognition and coordination support familiar submaximal execution despite one short night.

dose.opening_gate: Five minutes of easy carpark braking, corner entry, and bike-body separation, followed by the first 10-15 minutes of the Twin Peaks climb at RPE 2-3. Continue only with normal visual scanning, coordination, steering precision, breathing-to-RPE, and early line choice.
dose.climb: Complete one controlled climb to Twin Peaks at RPE 3-4. Normal standing for traction is allowed; no maximal standing attack, sprint, threshold effort, or breath-catching surge.
dose.descent: One Pure Quill descent on the familiar reference line at approximately 70-75 percent execution speed. Prioritize dynamically centred posture, early line choice, deliberate brake release, and stable front tracking.
dose.egress: Use only the required partial DH-Line egress at transport pace, then end the session.
dose.hard_cap: One climb, one Pure Quill descent, required egress, and 60-75 minutes elapsed. No second stage or substitute route.
dose.load_intent: Low-to-moderate training cost; session RPE 3-5, with no attempt to repair ACWR in one ride.

session.adaptation_hypothesis: A single clean familiar descent after a low-consequence field gate should refresh trail timing and centred-bike mechanics without the decision-quality risk created by speed, novelty, repeat density, or stacked setup variables under acute short sleep.
execution_rules: Pass the opening gate before committing to Twin Peaks; excellent motivation cannot substitute for normal coordination and decision timing.
Pure Quill only. Exclude TnT, Flintstone, 2K+, the full DH Line, jumps or doubles, novel aggressive lines, race pace, and setup testing.
Keep suspension, tyre pressure, cockpit, and cleat settings unchanged.
Use familiar braking markers and the familiar line; no segment time, chasing another rider, or speed target.
Finish after the required egress even if the first descent feels exceptional.
For a ride extending beyond 60 minutes in afternoon heat, target roughly 30-45 g carbohydrate per hour and 500-750 ml fluid per hour; record actual sodium rather than inventing it.

expected_result.technical: Wide vision, early line choice, deliberate braking, stable front tracking, and normal bike-body separation from the opening gate through egress, with no unforced correction or late fade.
expected_result.physiology: Climb remains RPE 3-4, whole-session RPE 3-5, and the ride does not become threshold, sprint, or repeatability work.
expected_result.next_day: Sunday Sabbath with no unusual cognitive, upper-body, or autonomic cost from the capped exposure.

stop_rules: Turn back during the opening gate for narrowed vision, delayed scanning, unexpected steering or foot correction, weak/heavy feel, or RPE that does not match the easy dose.
Do not descend Pure Quill if braking-marker recall, line anticipation, or coordination feels even subtly delayed at the top.

End technical intent for reactive braking, delayed line choice, rearward freezing, front-wheel deflection requiring emergency recovery, an unforced line miss, a near miss, or confidence outrunning precision.
Downshift and take the safest direct exit if climb RPE exceeds 5, breathing becomes disproportionate, upper-body fatigue exceeds 3/10, or heat/trail conditions exceed the session purpose.
The first Pure Quill descent ends the quality dose; no second climb, other stage, jump progression, sprint, or setup change.
